title: Majestic Save
transcript: I was just losing this position, but then something pretty incredible happened. In this position, the engine thinks that I had a chance to equalize, but the way to do that is absolutely incredible. And in the game, I did find the first move. Queen to F7, placing my queen right into the dragon's den and pressuring all of these key squares. But after black captured my bishop, I took this knight and after he took this pawn, he simply went on to win the game. But what else could I have done? There is no way for the knights to come in. Both of these jumps are covered by the pawn and this pawn, although attacked twice by my pieces, is defended three times by the black pieces. So, I could not see the utterly majestic move that would have allowed me to draw this game. Too beautiful. Knight takes G6, a move that looks like a blunder. This can be captured two different ways and the king is also pressuring that square. First and foremost, black [music] cannot ignore the knight, of course. If he does, now after knight H5, I am threatening a checkmate in one [music] and if black defends it with the knight, this is an incredible smothered mate using the pin of the queen on the bishop. But okay, so what? Black can simply take that knight, right? Well, he kind of has to, but no matter which way black takes, on our next move, we are free to play knight to H5 again. We are still threatening this checkmate and this time, if black tries to defend with the knight, we actually have a check and then a checkmate defended by the knight. And incredibly, the queen has no path to defend the G7 square. The only square that would have allowed that is G5, but now, of course, there is a black knight standing in the way. So, this would just be a checkmate. So, the beauty of this capture by white is that it's actually forcing black to checkmate itself. After knight to h5, either the f or e knight is going to be the one betraying the wrong king. And actually, the only way for white to hold on in this position is to give back the queen with a check. And conveniently, the knight on h5 can defend against this check. But now, three pieces against one queen should be enough for black to hold the draw.
